human_owner.summary: Approved in advance by the owner through auto mode; the Claude reviewer decides.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The frames show a small change in upper-arm angle between the start and end positions, so the upper arms are not perfectly still. shoulder_position_hold models this adequately and is arguably the best available choice. It gives the clavicular deltoid 0.35 as a stabilizer, which is plausible and not materially wrong.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: No change needed. Optionally, a future revision could consider a small assist-level glenohumeral action if the source clearly showed shoulder motion.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The grip and wrist_stability demands add many low-coefficient hand and forearm stabilizers (coefficients 0.035 to 0.35). This is how the tracer spreads the demand weights and is acceptable for a hand-held cable bar. It is not a definition error.

model_reviewer.summary: The definition fits the source. It is a bilateral lying incline cable triceps extension on a high pulley with a straight bar and a narrow overhand grip. The frames show the elbows flexed with the hands behind the head at the start and the arms extended at the end, so elbow_joint/extension is the single primary action. The tracer output matches: all three triceps heads are primary on both sides, with anconeus as a synergist. The shoulder_position_hold, grip and wrist_stability demands put the deltoid, forearm and hand muscles in the right places for a load held in the hands with the upper arms held still. The incline bench supports the trunk, so leaving out trunk bracing demands is reasonable. The labels open_chain, bilateral and elbow_extension are appropriate.
